selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: At Maghrib time, who does the person turn to?
questions.answer: He turns to Allah, the One who always lives and always remains.

questions.question: What does saying that Allah is greater than everything help a person do with worldly things?
questions.answer: It helps the person turn away from things that do not last.

questions.question: When the person stands with folded hands, what is he doing?
questions.answer: He is serving and worshipping his Lord.

questions.question: What does the person do after praising Allah?
questions.answer: He says that only Allah is worshipped and only Allah is asked for help.

questions.question: In bowing, what does the person admit about himself?
questions.answer: He admits that he is weak, needy, and small before Allah.

questions.question: In prostration, what does the person leave behind?
questions.answer: He leaves everything other than Allah.

questions.question: What does the person find when he humbles himself before Allah?
questions.answer: He finds the Most Compassionate Eternal Lord.

questions.question: What big idea about Maghrib prayer is taught in this passage?
questions.answer: It teaches that Maghrib prayer turns the heart away from temporary things and toward Allah.

questions.question: Why does the human spirit turn toward Allah at Maghrib?
questions.answer: Because the heart wants lasting beauty, and Allah alone is everlasting.

questions.question: What does the passage say Allah does with the great worlds?
questions.answer: He changes and moves them as He wills.

questions.question: What is a person showing by saying words of praise to Allah?
questions.answer: He is honoring Allah’s perfect greatness, beauty, and mercy.

questions.question: Who alone should we ask for help?
questions.answer: Allah alone.

questions.question: Why does the person bow in prayer?
questions.answer: To show humility before Allah’s power and greatness.

questions.question: What feelings are shown in prostration?
questions.answer: Love, wonder, worship, and deep humility.

questions.question: What is said about Allah when the person praises Him in sujood?
questions.answer: That Allah is far above weakness, loss, and any flaw.

questions.question: Which lasts forever in this passage: worldly things or Allah?
questions.answer: Allah lasts forever.

questions.question: At this prayer time, what kind of things does the person move away from?
questions.answer: He moves away from passing things that fade away.

questions.question: Why is Allah the right One to face in worship according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because He never dies, never changes, and always remains.

questions.question: What does the person do with his hands when he begins serving Allah?
questions.answer: He brings them together in worship.

questions.question: What two things does the person do with his words before bowing?
questions.answer: He praises Allah and asks Allah alone for help.

questions.question: What does bowing teach the person about himself and Allah?
questions.answer: It teaches that the person is weak and Allah is mighty.

questions.question: What does the person do with everything besides Allah during prostration?
questions.answer: He lets go of it and turns only to Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage describe Allah’s mercy?
questions.answer: It shows Allah as full of compassion and mercy without limit.

questions.question: What is one main lesson a student can learn from this passage?
questions.answer: We should love Allah most and worship Him with humble hearts.
